videos.title: Why Hawaii’s Islands Aren’t Connected by Boats 🚢 Ocean Mystery 🌊
videos.description:
Hawaii travel hides a surprising fact,  you can’t move between the islands by 🚢 boat! The 8 main Hawaiian Islands, 6 open to visitors, welcome 6 million tourists each year. Yet interisland travel is almost entirely by ✈️ plane, with just one small ferry between Maui and Lanai. Why? The distances are longer than they seem 📏 and the 🌊 Pacific Ocean is deep, wild, and unpredictable. For example, going from Oahu to the Big Island is 185 miles ⏱️ 30 hours by boat but only ✈️ 50 minutes by air. Hawaii is the only 🇺🇸 U.S. state fully surrounded by the Pacific, with storms 🌪️ strong currents 💨 and massive waves 🌊 In 2007, the 🚢 Hawaii Superferry launched with space for 900 passengers 👥 and 200 vehicles 🚗 But it shut down in just a few years due to 🌿 environmental concerns: fragile ecosystems, 🐋 whale migration, and invasive species. Many argue the real reason was political pressure and competition from ✈️ airlines, 🚗 rental car companies, and local transport.
Hawaii’s  geography,  isolation, and unique ecosystems make it one of the most fascinating  and challenging places for interisland travel.

videos.title: World’s Highest Bridge 😱 Huajiang Canyon in China 🌍
videos.description:
In China’s Guizhou province, something incredible is being built high above the Huajiang Grand Canyon 🇨🇳  By 2025, this breathtaking structure will become the tallest bridge in the world — rising 🏗️ 625 meters above the canyon floor, almost twice as tall as the 🗼 Eiffel Tower!
This part of China is already the world capital of mega-bridges 🌍 — home to 90 of the 100 highest bridges ever built. Why? Because the land here is extreme ⛰️: endless gorges, canyons, and mountains where building ordinary roads is nearly impossible. Engineers blast tunnels through cliffs and carve pathways across sheer rock walls 🚧 For now, the record belongs to the 🌉 Beipanjiang Bridge at 565 meters. But soon, the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge will take the crown 👑 stretching more than 1,400 meters across the canyon and connecting remote mountain regions. A true marvel of modern engineering ⚙️✨ and a symbol of human determination to conquer nature’s toughest challenges.

videos.title: The Most Complicated Border 😱 Town in Belgium & Netherlands 🇧🇪🇳🇱 Baarle
videos.description:
One of the most unusual borders in the world 🌍 In the small town of Baarle, you can cross between the Netherlands and Belgium 🇳🇱🇧🇪 more than 30 times in just 5 km 🚶‍♂️Inside Dutch territory lie 22 Belgian enclaves, and inside those — another 7 Dutch enclaves! The border runs right through streets 🚗  cafés ☕ shops 🛍️ and even private homes 🏠 Every plot of land follows the laws of its own country. That means in the Netherlands, beer is allowed from 18 🍺 but in Belgium — from 16 and Dutch teens definitely know it 😉 Some residents have even moved their front doors just to switch countries and pay less tax 💰 This bizarre patchwork goes back to the 12th century, when two feudal lords 🤝 traded, gifted and rented land like pieces of a mosaic. When Belgium and the Netherlands were eventually formed, they decided to keep the borders exactly as they were — leaving us with one of the strangest frontiers on Earth 🌏

videos.title: They Dragged 70 Warships Over a Mountain #history #animation #geography #historical #funny #shorts
videos.description:
In 1453 the Ottomans hauled about seventy warships out of the water, dragged them over the hill behind the Golden Horn, and put them back in on the other side. It was the least strange thing that happened that week.

Constantinople sat on a triangle of land. Two sides were water. The third was the great land walls, which no army had broken in a thousand years. The one weak point was the northern harbour, so the defenders sealed it with an iron chain — and as long as that chain held, the soft side of the city was safe.

Mehmed II went around it. This is how the city actually fell: a fortress built on the strait in four months, a bronze cannon twenty-seven feet long that sixty oxen had to move, a wall that was broken every day and rebuilt every night, and a small gate somebody left unlocked.

Built as an animated map — every route, wall, fortress and army position is placed on the real geography.

videos.title: This Island Exposes Earth's Deepest Secrets! 🌍🐧
videos.description:
🌍 This Island Exposes Earth's Deepest Secrets! 🐧😱

What if there was an island where rocks from deep inside Earth's mantle are exposed right on the surface?

Welcome to Macquarie Island, one of the most extraordinary geological locations on Earth!

📍 Located in the Southern Ocean between Australia and Antarctica, this remote island is only 34 kilometers long and 5 kilometers wide.

But its real mystery lies deep beneath the ocean!

🌋 Unlike ordinary volcanic islands, Macquarie Island contains a rare, intact section of oceanic crust and Earth's upper mantle.

🌎 Beneath the island, the Indo-Australian and Pacific tectonic plates grind against each other, pushing the seafloor upward.

⏳ Millions of years of geological forces created this incredible island, which is still slowly rising today.

🐧 And that's not all!

Macquarie Island is home to incredible penguin colonies, seals, and seabirds.

🌿 After invasive rats, mice, and rabbits were eradicated, the island was declared free of these pests in 2014, giving its fragile ecosystem a chance to recover.

🔬 Scientists are also studying seismic waves beneath the island to understand Earth's hidden geological structure and investigate whether a new subduction zone could be developing.

videos.title: Israel - Evolution on a map since WWI
videos.description:
Long video: https://youtu.be/Uqun0J23f6o

This video without voiceover shows the recent historical evolution of Israel.

1914: World War I – The United Kingdom and the Ottoman Empire clash.
1920: Treaty of Sèvres – The Ottoman Empire is dismantled in favor of the United Kingdom and France.
1921: The United Kingdom creates Transjordan and retains Palestine.
1947: UN Partition Plan for Palestine – The UN votes to partition the territory into two states, with Jerusalem under international control.
1948: Israeli Declaration of Independence – Neighboring Arab countries go to war against the new state.
1949: End of the Arab-Israeli War – Arab territories are shared among Israel, Egypt, and Jordan.
1967: Six-Day War – Israel occupies the Sinai, the Golan Heights, the Gaza Strip, the West Bank, and East Jerusalem.
1982: Peace with Egypt – Israel returns the Sinai.
1982: Operation Peace for Galilee – Israel militarily occupies southern Lebanon.
1988: Palestinian Declaration of Independence proclaimed by Yasser Arafat in Algiers.
2000: End of the occupation of southern Lebanon.
2005: End of the occupation of the Gaza Strip.

videos.description:

For most of the twentieth century the United States ran a strip of Panama as its own, then handed it over for nothing at noon on 31 December 1999.
Panama only exists as a country because Theodore Roosevelt wanted a canal, and the canal only works because it rains: every ship drains about 200 million liters of fresh water from Gatun Lake. In 1964 riots over a flag killed more than twenty people and pushed Washington into the 1977 Torrijos-Carter Treaties. Now Trump says "we're taking it back", and in February 2026 Panama threw Hong Kong's CK Hutchison out of the ports at both ends of the canal. Fifteen facts, in story order, explain it.

Why Is Germany Cutting Healthcare to Pay for Weapons?

Germany is preparing one of the biggest transformations of its public spending in decades. The country wants to significantly increase its investment in defense, while at the same time facing a weak economy, growing pressure on its healthcare system, an aging population, and an increasingly burdensome debt load.

In this video, we analyze why the German government is considering cuts to the welfare state, the role played by Europe’s new geopolitical environment, and why Germany’s challenge goes far beyond military spending.

Can Germany preserve its social model while financing a new era of rearmament and public debt?

videos.title: The growing problem of 'permanent car loans'
videos.description:
Car loans are getting longer in the U.S., and buyers are staying in debt longer.

Part of the reason is that cars have gotten much more expensive, but some buyers are also trading in their cars before they’ve finished paying them off and rolling that debt into their next loan. Today, nearly 1 in 4 buyers trading in a car worth less than what they still owe are underwater by $10,000 or more, according to a research by Edmunds.

Watch more on what’s causing the “permanent car debt” trap in the related video.

videos.title: 5 signs getting back with your ex could actually work this time
videos.description:
Is getting back with your ex ever a good idea?

Psychologist Sabrina Romanoff’s answer always follows the same formula: specific behavior change + a new plan for addressing the original problem + two people who feel secure on their own = a successful reunion.

Time, alone, isn’t a reliable variable in this equation, and most of the time that distance only makes people forget the lessons they learned the first time around, says Romanoff.

Here are five signs that reuniting with your ex could actually work.

videos.title: I run a pizzeria out of my Smart car in NYC
videos.description:
Bradley Alvelo, 38, runs Pizza Pod, a mobile pizzeria he operates out of a Smart car in New York CIty. After getting laid off from a corporate kitchen, Alvelo built the business from scratch.

He shares more on what it’s like running his pizza business out of his Smart car in related video.

videos.description:

In October 2018, they purchased their brownstone in Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn for about $1.5 million. The couple did a bulk of the renovation themselves and estimate they spent around $312,000 on it.

videos.title: How Jack Links built an ad campaign that grew its sales by 47% within 2 years
videos.description:
Link Snacks CEO Troy Link says the business was bringing in more than $300 million in annual sales in the early 2000s.

Around that time, Link was set on nailing a unique and splashy national marketing campaign to tell customers that the family-owned Jack Link’s wasn’t just another “big corporate-America brand,” he says.

Along with Minneapolis-based ad agency Carmichael Lynch, Link Snacks built an ad campaign around brazen protagonists fueling up with meat snacks before antagonizing an irritated-yet-intimidating Sasquatch alongside the tagline: “Feed your wild side.” The ads went viral on YouTube a year after the streaming platform launched, and the company started paying for them to air nationally in 2006.

Watch more about how Jack Link became a $1.6 billion/year business in the related video.

They renovated the backyard and added a pool and also opened an art studio in the small village where they now live. They now plan to open their home and studio to travelers looking for an authentic Andalusian experience.

videos.title: This 32-year-old earns $88K near New Haven, CT

videos.title: This family business went from bankrupt to $1.6B/year in sales
videos.description:
The first time Jack Link cured a batch of beef jerky, he was trying to save his business.

It was 1985 and Link was a 40-year-old father of two teens living in Minong, Wisconsin. The slaughterhouse he’d bought from family members in 1978 had just filed for bankruptcy protection. Its failure left him searching for a way to provide for his wife and children, and prove that he could turn a small family-run business into something bigger.

After a hunting trip, Troy Link says he brought home a few packs of convenience store jerky, prompting his father to examine the price tag. Based on the elder Link’s experience raising cattle and selling meat at his family’s general store over the years, he wondered whether his family business could make and sell its own version for less.

Today, meat snacks — including beef sticks and steak strips — form the core of Link Snacks’ multibillion-dollar global portfolio. See how they built their business into what it is today in related video.

videos.description:
Jacob Komarow ("Roy Donk") turned a $50 baklava experiment at a Phish concert into Good Baklava, a New York City business that averages just over $20,000 in monthly sales. Instead of opening a traditional storefront, Komarow sells Turkish baklava in parks, at beaches, concerts and music festivals, while also running an e-commerce and wholesale business. After overcoming drug addiction and entering sobriety with thousands of dollars in debt, Komarow says Good Baklava has become his “ticket out.”

videos.title: How do you know when it's time to leave a relationship?
videos.description:
Clinical psychologist Sabrina Romanoff has worked with couples for a decade — and she can tell a relationship has run its course if she consistently hears these 5 key phrases.

These phrases are particularly insidious because while they might seem like valid points on the surface, they are often used to avoid accountability and sow uncertainty.

videos.title: 4 things that are worth the money
videos.description:
Videos on TikTok of users sharing the items they swear are “always” worth the money have racked up hundreds of thousands of views and likes this summer.

CNBC Make It asked money pros for items they think are worth the money. Here’s what they had to say.

videos.title: Are you living the American Dream?
videos.description:
The American Dream, much like the country it inspires, is in a state of constant change.

Ask 100 people what the ideal means to them, and you’ll likely get just as many answers. Most might agree, for example, that the American Dream includes achieving financial stability or being happy, but what that looks like is more individual.

To recognize the country’s 250th year, CNBC Make It got notable voices in politics, finance and relationships across age ranges to sit down and spark conversation about what it means to achieve happiness and success in this country today.

More on their thoughts in the related video.

videos.title: Is the American Dream realistic for everyone?
videos.description:
To recognize the country’s 250th year, CNBC Make It got notable voices in politics, finance and relationships across age ranges to sit down and spark conversation about what it means to achieve happiness and success in this country today.

Vivian Tu, 32, a self-made millionaire and founder of financial education brand Your Rich BFF, spoke with Sylvia Kwan, 62, CEO of financial services firm Ellevest. Here’s their thoughts on what the American Dream is — and if it’s realistic for everyone.

videos.title: Do you feel hopeful about the future of the U.S.?
videos.description:
Gen Zers have seen their education and social growth stunted by the Covid-19 pandemic, and those who’ve graduated high school or college have entered a volatile workforce, only to find an out-of-reach housing market and inflationary pressures.

To recognize the country’s 250th year, CNBC Make It got notable voices in politics, finance and relationships across age ranges to sit down and spark conversation about what it means to achieve happiness and success in this country today.

As the youngest member of our cohort, 26-year-old history newsletter writer and social media creator Kahlil Greene says he doesn’t feel hopeful for the future of the U.S. and worries the country is on a “downward trajectory.”

Robert Reich holds the opposite view. “I’m optimistic because of our resilience,” the 80-year-old University of California, Berkeley professor and former U.S. labor secretary told Greene.

What are your thoughts on the future of the United States?

videos.title: How Costco keeps gas so cheap
videos.description:
As Americans look to save money at the pump, many are turning to Costco.

One analysis found Costco sells gasoline at about a 9-cent discount to major local competitors and roughly 24 cents below statewide averages. But cheap gas is just one part of Costco’s bigger strategy and a key driver of the company’s profitability.

More on why Costco keeps gas prices so low in the related video.

videos.title: I bring in $2.3M/year negotiating car deals
videos.description:
Tomi Mikula, 33, is the founder and CEO of Delivrd, a remote business that negotiates car deals. Mikula worked at a car dealership for 6 years before starting his business in 2023. He says Delivrd closed 2,300 deals in 2025 and its average savings per deal is about $6,300.

Take a look at how he built his business into what it is today in the related video.

videos.title: How Imax Makes Millions From Theaters It Doesn't Own
videos.description:
Christopher Nolan’s "The Odyssey" just became the highest-grossing Imax release of all time. And now, months before "Dune: Part Three" hits theaters, demand for its Imax 70mm screenings crashed ticketing sites and sent fans lining up outside theaters. The frenzy is good business for Imax. In 2025, it generated about $410 million in revenue, despite representing roughly 1% of movie screens worldwide.

videos.title: Why everyone's so obsessed with 'maxxing' right now
videos.description:
Adding more books to your reading list this year? You’re booksmaxxing. Changing your appearance to become more attractive? Looksmaxxing.

Across social media, it seems like just about everything can be “maxxed” these days. Whatever your hobby, habit or goal, the objective is not to just do it, but to maximize it to its full potential. And as consumers look for new ways to improve themselves, more companies are paying attention.

More on why “maxxing” has become so popular — and why the viral trends concern some mental health experts — in the related video.

videos.title: Is buying a home still the American Dream?
videos.description:
Is buying a home still the American Dream?

CNBC Make It spoke with renters around the country — millionaires, former homeowners, forever renters — for their thoughts. Watch more on why renting is growing more attractive than buying in the U.S. in the related video.

videos.title: Is location sharing practical, romantic or controlling?
videos.description:
There are plenty of device-dependent gestures that hold weight during a flourishing romance.

Sharing your location with your partner is one such gesture. Some call location-sharing a “love language,” and others have noted that it feels like a step towards deeper intimacy.

There’s no rule that a healthy relationship requires sharing your location with your partner — but discomfort with your partner knowing where you are or vice versa is something to talk about.

videos.title: Is marriage still worth it?
videos.description:
For generations, marriage was considered a key part of the American Dream.

But that trend is quickly changing for younger Americans, especially women: Just 33% of Gen Z women say marriage is integral to achieving the American Dream, compared with 43% of Gen Z men, according to a new CNBC and SurveyMonkey survey.

Despite marriage’s association with greater wealth and happiness, the potential benefits aren’t enough for some younger Americans to make it an immediate priority.

videos.description:
After Hamburg’s failed bid to host the 2024 Olympic Games, two-time Olympic gold medalist Moritz Fürste helped build HYROX with no plan B.

Bavishi, 42, is the founder and CEO of Brooklyn, New York-based ice cream company Malai, which she founded in 2015. The business — which operates four brick-and-mortar locations across New York, Philadelphia and Washington D.C., plus a growing wholesale and e-commerce business — brought in $2.8 million in total sales in 2025, according to documents reviewed by CNBC Make It.

See how she built her business into what it is today in the related video.

videos.title: Is buying a home still a cornerstone of the American Dream?
videos.description:
Owning a home has long been part of the American Dream. But in the country’s 250th year, many Americans feel the goal, a milestone of adulthood and a marker of financial success, eludes them.

Housing prices, borrowing costs and homeownership expenses are high. While homeowners can still build long-term wealth through their properties, experts say amassing equity can take longer today than it did for buyers in previous decades, given higher expenses and decelerating home value appreciation in today’s market conditions.

CNBC Make It spoke with renters around the country — millionaires, former homeowners, forever renters — for their thoughts on whether owning a home is still a part of their American Dream. See what their thoughts were in the related video.

videos.title: This couple quit their film and PR careers to take over family's cemetery business
videos.description:
Shayda Frost and Timothy Amoui sometimes joke that they work in “innovative real estate.” After all, as Frost puts it, a burial plot is essentially “a very, very small bit of land that you own forever.”

Frost, 39, and Amoui, 36, are the owners of Lincoln Memorial Group, a cemetery company that operates four working cemeteries in Atlanta. In 2025, the company brought in about $6.3 million in revenue and made about $1.7 million in net income, according to documents reviewed by CNBC Make It. The business has brought in an average of nearly $6 million a year between 2021 and 2025.

Take a look at what it’s like running a cemetery business in the related video.

videos.title: Are Stablecoins The Future Of Money?
videos.description:

Some analysts estimate the Stablecoin market could grow from roughly $300 billion today to $1.45 trillion by 2035. But what exactly are stablecoins, and why is there so much hype surrounding them on Wall Street?

videos.description:
That EMI could cost more than expected.

The RBI’s decision to raise the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.5% can have a direct impact on borrowing, saving and spending across the economy.

The repo rate is the interest rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities. When this rate goes up, the cost of borrowing for banks can increase, and that can eventually affect the rates offered to customers.

For someone planning a big purchase on EMI, such as a car, house, phone or laptop, higher lending rates can make the overall cost of borrowing more expensive. Existing floating-rate home loans can also see changes in EMI amounts or loan tenure, depending on how the bank passes on the rate hike.

There can also be an impact on personal loans, credit card EMI conversions and other forms of consumer borrowing. On the other side, higher interest rates can make fixed deposits and recurring deposits more attractive as banks look to encourage people to keep their money with them.

The impact does not stop with individual borrowers. Higher borrowing costs can make it more expensive for businesses to raise funds, which may lead companies to delay expansion, reduce new investments or become more cautious with hiring. This can eventually affect overall demand, business growth and job creation.

This video explains Debt Mutual Funds. Debt funds may look simple and safe, but choosing the wrong fund for your investment duration can expose you to credit risk, liquidity risk and interest rate risk.

In this video, you will learn what debt funds are, how bonds and fixed-income instruments work, different types of debt funds like overnight, liquid, ultra-short, money market, short-duration, corporate bond and banking & PSU funds, how credit ratings work, what Macaulay Duration means, how to match your investment horizon with the right fund, how debt funds are taxed, how they compare with FDs and arbitrage funds, and what exactly went wrong in the Franklin Templeton debt fund crisis. ALL in this one single video.

videos.description:
▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀
Checkout slice: https://slice-dp.onelink.me/pDW8/nuakig9t & Use code 'LLASEPT26' to get some rewards.

▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀

If you have ever wondered how RBI actually controls banks, inflation, interest rates and even your home loan EMI, then this is the ultimate RBI guide you need to understand how India’s central bank really works. RBI's decisions can directly impact your loans, investments, bank deposits and the entire economy

You will learn how RBI creates and controls money, the different measures RBI uses to manage India’s financial system, currency management and interventions during banking crises. We also cover real examples like the 2003 ICICI Bank panic, Yes Bank and PMC Bank crisis, demonetisation, RBI surplus transfers, the government vs RBI debate and India’s 1991 economic crisis. ALL in this one single video.
